title: swatplus-rust: SWAT+ translated from Fortran into Rust, verified bit for bit
description:
swatplus-rust is the SWAT+ (Soil and Water Assessment Tool Plus) hydrological model translated from Fortran into Rust: commit 6f51536 of SWAT+, with output tables identical bit for bit to SWAT+'s on two SWAT+ examples (Osu_1hru, Ames_sub1), two real catchments in West Sumatra, Indonesia (Batanghari, 1,858 HRUs; Pessel, 3,966 HRUs) and 33 variants that each exercise a feature. It runs natively and in the browser (WebAssembly), writes SWAT+'s text tables or Parquet, and depends only on rayon (for threads) beyond the Rust standard library; the simulation has no unsafe code (only the WebAssembly module's memory functions use it).

On a Snapdragon (ARM64) laptop it runs 2.6 to 2.9 times as fast as SWAT+ built as its project builds it, with half the memory on the large catchments, and the same results (docs/benchmark-results). Translating it brought out 136 catalogued behaviours of SWAT+ that the port keeps for identical results and 22 bugs of SWAT+ that an option (--fix-swat) corrects (docs/swat-quirks.md, docs/swat-fixes.md). A design note in Indonesian describes every function (docs/nota-desain: Markdown, Word, PDF).

Version 1.0.2 adds programs for Windows and Linux on ARM64; on the same laptop the two give byte-identical output for 19 of 20 tables, the last differing in 7 values of the diagnostic USLE column in the last printed digit. Version 1.0.3 prints the point source tables as SWAT+'s list-directed write does, so that all 2,079,406,557 values of the 37 validation scenarios are identical to SWAT+'s (docs/validation-results); its repository is public, without the private scenarios.

Version 1.1.0 runs a simulation a day at a time (it can be copied mid-run, for a spin-up run once), applies calibration changes in memory and runs batches of parameter sets one per core, and, with --fix-swat, runs the HRUs and the routing by sub-basin on several threads with the same tables for any number of threads (on a 12-core laptop a Batanghari-sized run takes 15.4 s on one thread and 9.2 s on twelve). Faithful runs are unchanged: every table of the 37 validation scenarios is the same as 1.0.3's. It adds tools for stage-based calibration (calibration/swatcal) and GSMaP precipitation.

Version 1.2.0 applies calibration changes to a running simulation between two days and can start every parameter set of a batch from one shared spin-up (batch --shared-spinup). A study with them on the two catchments (docs/spinup.md) finds two warm-up years enough for soil water and annual volumes, the shallow aquifers settling in two to three, and the ranking of parameter sets kept by a shared spin-up in one catchment (rank correlation 0.99) but not the other (0.77), for 14 to 16 % less time, so calibrations keep each run's own spin-up. The design note describes the engine as of this version. Faithful runs are unchanged.

Contributions. Andri Yanto conceived the project and directed it: the decisions of design (a faithful, verified translation; SWAT+'s quirks kept and documented, its bugs corrected only on request; dependencies kept to the minimum; the engine kept apart from the RustGIS editor under its own license), the choice and preparation of the validation catchments, the validation strategy, and the review of the results. The Rust code, the tests, the validation scripts and the documentation were written with Claude, an AI model by Anthropic (Claude Code, 2026), working under his direction; every change was checked against SWAT+ Fortran by the validation in continuous integration before it was kept.

The Batanghari and Pessel scenarios are private data and are not in this archive; SWAT+'s own scenarios are. SWAT+ is developed by USDA-ARS and Texas A&M AgriLife Research; this work is not affiliated with or endorsed by them.
